Subject: Post-incident summary and recommended mitigations — Live chat latency (ClearHarbor)

Hi Alex — thanks again for the quick reproduction and the traces. Below is a concise post-incident summary and recommended next steps.

Summary:
- Impact: token-delivery latency spikes on streaming/chat endpoints for ClearHarbor between 08:37–09:05 PDT on 2026-07-21.
- Root cause (short): increased memory pressure on serving nodes in us-west-2 caused elevated KV cache evictions and rehydration pauses; concurrent colocated workload amplified scheduling jitter.
- Customer impact: up to 10s chunk latency for ~120 active sessions; majority restored by temporary parameter change.

Immediate mitigations applied / recommended:
1) Temporary: ClearHarbor applied reduced max_tokens and chunk_size; this materially reduced tail latency (confirmed by client traces).
2) Routing: We placed ClearHarbor traffic on a warm pool (no colocated best-effort workloads) for the remainder of the day.
3) Autoscale tuning: Increased slow-path headroom on affected pool and added a temporary soft cap for colocated low-priority variants.

Next steps (action items):
- (RW-INC-427) Engineering will replace a noisy colocated model and apply a kernel-level change to reduce rehydration penalty — ETA: 2026-07-27.
- (RW-OPS-1124) Ops will add a KV cache miss alert threshold to catch 50%+ drop in hit rate and notify on-call — ETA: 2026-07-24.
- Customer play: If you prefer, we can keep the reduced max_tokens/chunk_size config for a rolling two-week window while the platform fix is deployed.

Attachments: postmortem-digest.pdf (summary + timelines) — shared to your ClearHarbor drive link above.

If you'd like a short 30-minute run-through of the postmortem and the mitigation options tomorrow, I'm happy to schedule. Thanks for your patience — we know latency on interactive flows is disruptive and we appreciate the fast feedback loops that helped narrow the fix.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
